entities.name: Franco-Turkish War
entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary:
The Franco-Turkish War was a pivotal conflict of the Turkish War of Independence, lasting from 1918 to 1921 in Cilicia, a region in what is now southern Turkey. 

 The war was fought between the Turkish nationalist forces, led by Mustafa Kemal Atatürk, and the French, who had occupied Cilicia after World War I. 

 The conflict was a crucial turning point in the establishment of the modern Turkish state, as it led to the eventual withdrawal of French forces and the declaration of the Republic of Turkey in 1923. 

 The war also had significant cultural and economic consequences, as it led to the displacement of many Armenians and Greeks from the region and the establishment of a new economic order in Turkey.
